AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To assess the safety of meningococcal group B (MenB)-4C vaccine.

AbstractText.Label: PARTICIPANTS
AbstractText.content: Undergraduates, dormitory residents, and persons with high-risk medical conditions received the MenB-4C vaccine two-dose series during mass vaccination clinics from 12/2013 through 11/2014.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Adverse events (AEs) were identified by 15 minutes of observation postvaccination, spontaneous reports, surveys, and hospital surveillance. Causality was assessed for serious adverse events (SAEs).

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: 16,974 persons received 31,313 MenB-4C doses. The incidence of syncope during the 15-minutes post-dose 1 was 0.88/1000 persons. 2% of participants spontaneously reported an AE (most common were arm pain and fever). 3 SAEs were suspected of being caused by the vaccine, including one case of anaphylaxis.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Most AEs reported were nonserious and consistent with previous clinical trial findings. Measures to prevent injury from syncope and to treat anaphylaxis should be available wherever vaccines are administered. Our safety evaluation supports the use of MenB-4C in response to outbreaks.
